podcast.title: 1972 Concert Review - U. Cutler
podcast.body: In a 1972 review in the Wilmington Delaware News Journal's "Under Thirty" section, U. Cutler called Poco "rock music's answer to Mother Nature's late afternoon sunshine rainbow," praising co-founder Rusty Young's pedal steel guitar, the band's perfect three-part harmonies, and Paul Cotton's lyrics, while lamenting their lack of wider recognition. "he called polko rock music's answer to mother nature's late afternoon sunshine rainbow."

podcast.title: "Kiss of Death" by Robert Hilburn
podcast.body: Robert Hilburn of the LA Times inadvertently gave Poco the "kiss of death" by referring to them as "the next big thing," a label that failed to materialize into mainstream success despite their loyal fanbase. "Robert Hillburn of the LA Times gave them the kiss of death by referring to them as the next big thing."

srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock
Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Country Rock Influence
podcast.body: Poco's influence on country rock is noted as similar to that of Gram Parsons, with their musical DNA present in the genre, even if they did not achieve the same level of fame as other bands. Pure Prairie League specifically stated they wanted to emulate Poco's sound after listening to them. "the band goes influence on country rock is similar to that of Graham Parsons the DNA is there even if they themselves did not achieve the level of fame as this other band that that's coming up."

Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Country Rock Vision
podcast.body: Rusty Young articulated the band's vision for country rock as combining Richie Furay's rock and roll melodies and voice with country instruments as a "palette to color that." "we had this idea of taking richies rock and roll melodies referring to richie puree and the songs he wrote in his voice and the palette to color that would be country instruments that was country rock."

srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock
Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Influential Country Rock Pioneer
podcast.body: Poco is considered one of the "descendants" of The Flying Burrito Brothers' seminal album "Gilded Palace of Sin," demonstrating its early influence on the country rock genre. The band also significantly influenced Pure Prairie League, who "wore out" Poco's first record from 1969, adopting their approach to blending rock with country elements and instruments. "But it's about its descendants. It's about polka and the eagles and the rolling stones." "polko had just come out with their first record in nineteen sixty nine and we individually wore those records out"

Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Marketing Challenges
podcast.body: Despite creating great songs, Poco struggled with widespread commercial success because their music did not fit neatly into typical radio formats, making them harder to market. "again it comes down to knowing how to market a band that does not neatly fit into a radio format."

Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Name Change Due to Cartoon
podcast.body: The band had to change their name from "Polko" to "Poco" to avoid legal conflicts with a cartoon of the same name. "they were polko but they had to change their name to avoid legal conflicts over the cartoon of the same name."

srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock
Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Non-Commercial Music
podcast.body: Rusty Young highlighted the difference between Poco and The Eagles by stating that The Eagles made commercial music that could be played on AM and country radio, whereas Poco never did. "the difference between picking up the pieces by polko and what the Eagles did is that the Eagles could be played on AM and country radio and polko could not they made commercial music and we never did."

Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: On the Verge of Being Dropped
podcast.body: Prior to their 1978 hit "Crazy Love," Poco's record label was on the verge of dropping them due to their lack of commercial breakthrough. "their record label was on the verge of dropping them when Timothy Schmidt left to go join the Eagles."

Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Original Name "Polko" Meaning
podcast.body: The band was originally named "Polko," which means "little" in Spanish, intentionally reflecting their identity as a "little four piece band." "polko and Spanish means little which was intentional it's the little four piece band."

podcast.title: Troubadour House Band
podcast.body: Poco served as the house band at the renowned Troubadour club. "polko was the house band at the troubadour."
